inputs.original_text: The Liberal Party is showing dangerous cracks from within, with some MPs floating leadership changes because Andrew Hastie wants to open the door to higher taxes on gas companies and stripping concessions from property investors. Angus Taylor has rightly slammed the door on those ideas, exposing the real philosophical clash with the opposition leader. The leader at least had the sense not to echo Hastie's attacks on Donald Trump, but his evasion on whether he will back the US and Israel against Iran is worrying. We cannot afford to drift toward bigger government and weak alliances if we are going to defend our traditions, personal responsibility, and national way of life.
inputs.modified_text: The Liberal Party is tearing itself apart from within, with some MPs pushing for a leadership change over Andrew Hastie's reckless proposals to hike taxes on gas companies and strip concessions from property investors. Angus Taylor has done the right thing by slamming the door on those ideas, laying bare the real divide with the opposition leader. At least the leader had the sense not to pile on Hastie's attacks against Donald Trump, but his refusal to clearly back the US and Israel against Iran shows dangerous weakness. This kind of drift toward bigger government and unreliable alliances threatens our national traditions, personal responsibility, and the way of life we must defend.
